channel.description: Latest articles from Dispute Resolution Review (drr.scholasticahq.com)

item.title: The Role of Mediation Institutions: Ensuring Enforceability Under Article 5 of the Singapore Convention on Mediation | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Wooseok SHIN. This article explores how mediation institutions can enhance the enforceability of international settlement agreements under the Singapore Convention on Mediation by addressing legal uncertainties through proactive involvement.

item.title: Enforcement of Arbitral Awards Obtained Against States on the Assets of State-Owned Entities: Reformulation of the English Approach | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Darius Chan, Amar Pandey. Sovereign immunity—discover how different jurisdictions and global shifts are reshaping the boundaries of protection of state-owned entities in international dispute resolution.

item.title: Operationalising the Social Licence to Operate along the Belt and Road: The Case for a Mediation-Focused Approach | Published in Dispute Resolution Review

item.title: The Conditional Benefit Doctrine and Assignees of Contractual Benefit under Contract and Commercial Law Act 2017 | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Jiufeng Chang. This article examines the impact of exclusive dispute resolutions on assignees of contractual benefit in New Zealand law with reference to the Contract and Commercial Law Act 2017.

item.title: Foreword: Bridging Polarised Discourse | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Adele Millard. Dr Adele Millard introduces this Special Edition: "Bridging Polarised Discourse".

item.title: Bridging the Divide: Insights into Australian Parents’ Vaccine Decision Making | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Elizabeth Fewster. Parents who reach different vaccination decisions nonetheless move through similar uncertainty, embodied knowledge and negotiations of biomedical authority, challenging vaccine binaries and opening new ways of understanding vaccine decision making.

item.title: The Politics of Voice and the Re-Integration of the Public Sphere: What Does Anthropology Have to Offer? | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Pascale Taplin, Tim Pilbrow. Australia’s 2023 Voice referendum exposed deep online polarisation, highlighting how echo chambers challenge public discourse and how ethnography can help bridge fractured worldviews.

item.title: Lewis Deep Democracy | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Myrna Lewis. Lewis Deep Democracy is a global conflict-resolution method that surfaces hidden tensions and fosters inclusive dialogue, illustrated through case studies showing its power to transform polarised, emotionally charged communities.

item.title: Bridging Individual and Community Needs: The Story Behind the Success of Australia’s First Co-Funded Inner Urban Co-Housing Development | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Alex Fearnside. Urban Coup’s 14-year journey created Australia’s first privately funded inner-urban co-housing community in Melbourne, blending sustainability, affordability, and connection.

item.title: Creating Mangroves: The Vibrant Living Space Between Polarised Others. A Reflection on My Encounters with Traditional Owners in the Native Title Setting | Published in Dispute Resolution Review
item.description: By Louise Allwood. Through a phenomenological lens I reflect on my lived experience working in the applied field of native title anthropology where I have bridged polarising discourses with traditional owners.
